perfect_tense.overview: El Pretérito Perfecto (Present Perfect) expresa una acción pasada que tiene relevancia al presente. La acción ocurrió en el pasado pero sus resultados o efectos continúan en el presente. Es muy común en España; en América Latina se usa más el pretérito simple.

uses.name: Recent Past Actions with Present Relevance
uses.description: Actions that happened recently and have a connection to the present; the action is finished but the results affect the now

examples.spanish: Hasta ahora he vivido 5 años en Ecuador.
examples.english: Until now, I have lived 5 years in Ecuador.
examples.explanation: An action that started in the past and continues/has relevance to the present. Used with 'hasta ahora' (until now)

examples.english: I have seen the Jumanji movie.
examples.explanation: Past action (watching the movie) with present relevance (I know what it's like)
Past experience that affects current knowledge

uses.name: This Week, Month, Year
uses.description: Actions that occurred within a time period that hasn't finished yet

examples.english: This week I have worked a lot.
examples.explanation: The week is still ongoing; used with time periods that are 'open'

examples.english: Today I have seen three movies.
examples.explanation: Today hasn't ended yet; we're still in it

examples.spanish: Este año hemos viajado a tres países.
examples.english: This year we have traveled to three countries.

uses.name: Personal Life Experiences
uses.description: Things you have done or experienced at some point in your life

examples.english: I have never traveled to Asia.

examples.spanish: He vivido en cinco ciudades diferentes.
examples.english: I have lived in five different cities.

uses.name: News or Recent Events
uses.description: Reporting something that just happened or news that is still 'fresh'

examples.spanish: Se ha ido sin decir nada.
examples.english: He has left without saying anything.

examples.spanish: Ha habido un accidente en la carretera.
examples.english: There has been an accident on the road.

perfect_vs_preterite.note: In Spain, perfect is very common for recent past. In Latin America, preterite is more common. They can often be interchangeable.
perfect_vs_preterite.spanish_usage: Spain uses perfect more; Latin America uses preterite more

example_comparison.perfect_english: This morning I have eaten bread. (Spain - more common)
example_comparison.preterite_english: This morning I ate bread. (Latin America - more common)
example_comparison.note: Both are grammatically correct; preference varies by region

example_sentences.spanish: Voy a merendar Pasta en bolsas de carne
example_sentences.english: I'm going to have an afternoon snack: Pasta with meat sacks

example_sentences.spanish: Tienes la máquina para hacer la pasta
example_sentences.english: You have the machine to make pasta

example_sentences.spanish: Yo me siento emocionado cuando los vela en el cine
example_sentences.english: I feel emotional when I see them at the cinema
I see them at the cinema

example_sentences.spanish: Mi sobrino cumple hoy veinte años
